description: Hand-labelled speech attribution (B2, SPEC-17). Every quoted span in `text` is listed in `lines`, in order, with its true speaker (a cast name) or null when no canon character says it. Covers inversions, plain and before tags, action beats, a pronoun tag with no beat, a beat naming two people, a strictly alternating untagged exchange, a speech continued across paragraphs, a split quote and non-cast speakers.
text:
The ferry docked at noon, and the three of them came down the ramp together.

“We are late,” said Ada Pell.

Bram Kestrel shrugged. “The tide does not care about our schedule.”

“Then the tide can carry the luggage,” Corin said, dropping her bag on the boards.

The porter frowned at the bag. “That will be two coins, miss,” he said.

Ada said, “Pay the man, Bram.”

“Because you lost the wager,” she said.

Corin turned to Ada at the top of the stairs.

“Did you bring the letter?” Corin asked.

“It is in my coat,” Ada answered.

“Show me.”

“Not here.”

“Then where?”

Bram cleared his throat. “When I was a boy on this island, the ferry ran twice a day, and nobody ever asked for a letter.

“Now they want papers for everything.”

“Papers,” said Corin Vale, “are how the island remembers.”

“Enough,” Ada said. “We go up.”

Bram looked at Corin. “After you.”

“Very gallant,” said Ms. Pell.

“Mind the gap in the third step,” called the porter from below.

held_out.description: Held-out lines, written before the wave-1 review fixes (B1/B2) changed the rules and never used to tune them. Adversarial shapes: `said X to Y` and `X told/asked Y` with a non-cast speaker, a before-tag `said to Y`, pronoun tags after a beat whose subject is the other gender, a vocative, a cast speaker addressing someone (`said Corin to the porter`), a beat naming a place, and a beat whose subject is a non-cast noun. Same cast as the main set; reported separately from the 20 in-sample lines.
held_out.text:
“Read the manifest first,” said the harbourmaster to Bram.

“Not today,” the old man told Corin.

“Is it far?” the porter asked Ada.

The clerk said to Bram, “Sign here.”

Bram looked at her across the table. “Sit down before you fall down,” she said.

Corin slammed the ledger shut. “Fine,” he said.

Ada pushed the coins back to him. “Count them again,” he said.

The gulls wheeled over the quay.

“Corin, run,” Bram said.

“Bram,” Corin said.

“Sign it,” Ada said to the clerk.

“Then go,” said Corin to the porter.

“Where is the key?” Bram asked Ada.

Ada crossed to the Harbour Office. “Wait here.”

The porter nodded to Ada. “As you like.”

Bram shrugged. “Suit yourself.”

“Leave the ledger,” said the auditor to Corin.

“Hush,” said Ada to Corin.
